stem: A microcontroller in an irrigation system at a farm near Chinhoyi stores data in 8-bit and 16-bit registers.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Explain why the microcontroller stores all data in binary.

points.description: It is made of switches/transistors/logic gates that have two states (on/off).
The two states represent 1 and 0, so all data must be converted to binary to be processed and stored.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The microcontroller's circuits are made of transistors that act as switches with only two states. These states represent the binary digits 1 and 0, so data must be held in binary to be processed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: A 16-bit register holds the denary value 2748. Give this value in hexadecimal.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Convert the hexadecimal value 9E to 8-bit binary.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Add the 8-bit binary integers 01101011 and 01010110. Give an 8-bit answer.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: The 8-bit integers 11001010 and 01100111 are added. Give the 8 bits left in the register.
parts.explanation: The full sum is 100110001 (305); the register keeps 00110001.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Explain why the result in (e) is incorrect.

points.description: The true sum (305) is greater than 255, so it needs 9 bits; the extra bit is lost (overflow).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: 202 + 103 = 305, which is more than 255, the largest 8-bit value, so the ninth bit is lost: an overflow error.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Carry out a logical right shift of 2 places on 11001100. Give the 8-bit result.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Describe the effect of the shift in (g) on the value stored.

points.description: It divides the value by 4 (204 → 51); here the result is exact because only 0s were shifted out.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The value is divided by 4, from 204 to 51; the two bits lost were 0s, so no remainder is lost.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: A temperature of -57 is stored in 8-bit two's complement. Give the binary value.

parts.label: (j)
parts.stem: Another register holds the two's complement value 10110101. Give its denary value.

parts.label: (k)
parts.stem: Identify one place, other than memory dumps, where hexadecimal is used.

points.description: Any one: MAC addresses; HTML colour codes; error codes; assembly language / memory addresses.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: MAC addresses of network cards.

hints: Group 16 bits into nibbles for hexadecimal.
Two's complement: positive in 8 bits, invert, add 1; the MSB is worth −128.

stem: A tourism company in Victoria Falls makes short promotional clips with recorded commentary and still photos for its website.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how the commentary is stored as binary.

points.description: The amplitude/height of the sound wave is measured (sampled) at regular time intervals.
Each sample is stored as a binary number using a fixed number of bits (the sample resolution).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The sound wave's amplitude is sampled at set intervals, and each measurement is rounded and stored as a binary number using the sample resolution's number of bits.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What is the effect of increasing the sample resolution?

options.content: More accurate sound and a smaller file
options.rationale: More bits per sample makes the file larger.

options.content: More accurate sound and a larger file
options.rationale: Correct: more levels per sample, more bits stored.

options.content: Less accurate sound and a larger file
options.rationale: More bits per sample gives more accuracy.

parts.explanation: Higher resolution → more possible levels → more accurate, but each sample uses more bits.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The commentary is recorded for 45 seconds at 16384 Hz with a sample resolution of 8 bits. Calculate the file size in KiB. Show your working.
parts.explanation: Bits $= 16384 \times 8 \times 45$; bytes $= 16384 \times 45$ (8-bit samples are 1 byte); KiB $= 16 \times 45 = 720$ (since 16384 = 16 × 1024).
parts.workedSolution: 1. Bits $= 16384 \times 8 \times 45$; bytes $= 16384 \times 45$ (8-bit samples are 1 byte); KiB $= 16 \times 45 = 720$ (since 16384 = 16 × 1024).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: A logo uses 100 different colours. State the smallest colour depth that can be used.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: A photo is 2560 × 1200 pixels with a colour depth of 24 bits. Calculate its file size in KiB.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: The photos load slowly on phones. Describe one lossy method that could reduce the photos' file size and its effect on photo quality.

points.description: Method: reduce the resolution (fewer pixels) or reduce the colour depth (fewer bits per pixel).
Effect: the data is permanently removed, so the photo has less detail / fewer colours (lower quality), but a smaller file.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Reduce the colour depth from 24 to 8 bits per pixel. The file becomes a third of the size, but each pixel can only be one of 256 colours, so shading looks less smooth and the lost data cannot be recovered.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: One row of the company logo has the pixel colours R R R R R R R R R R G G G G G R R R R R R B B B. Write the row using run-length encoding as count then colour (for example 3B).

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: The company's price list is a spreadsheet that is emailed to agents. Explain why it should be compressed with lossless rather than lossy compression.

points.description: Lossless compression lets the original be rebuilt exactly.
Every price/value in the spreadsheet must be exactly right; lossy would permanently remove/change data.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: With lossless compression the spreadsheet is rebuilt exactly when it is decompressed. Lossy compression would permanently remove data, which could change or lose prices, so it is unsuitable.

hints: File sizes: work in bits, then ÷ 8 and ÷ 1024; cancel before multiplying.
RLE: count each run of the same colour.
